requirements.text: To stop the plugin's documented high and medium security gaps from being exploited, the business must close gaps 2, 3, and 6 of the LLM security checklist and add a blocking guardrail layer.
To make governance sign-offs trustworthy, the business must back every gate and approval with verified evidence and keep a tamper-evident audit log.
To let adopters use the plugin under SOC 2, HIPAA, and FERPA, the business must provide compliance profiles built on one attributable audit trail.
To assign ownership and review cadence for every control, the business must map controls to the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 and the NIST AI RMF functions.
To catch defects early without alert fatigue, the business must route findings by severity, blocking only high-confidence, high-severity ones.

To know whether each release makes the coding and spec-writing agents better or worse, the business must measure their output on in-house golden tasks, graded by execution for code and by checklist plus an optional separate judge for specs, and track the scores release over release. (Group A, DRAFT)

To shorten review rounds and keep reviewer findings trustworthy, the business must give reviewers named checklists, a round-by-round iteration record, fixed-severity findings, and a feedback loop from the user's labels to checklist changes. (Group B, DRAFT)
The plugin user shall be able to rely on a PR verdict being posted only after the user's recorded confirmation, even when attacker-controlled PR text is in the session.
The plugin user shall be able to commit and push without staging secrets or pushing to an unexpected remote.
The maintainer shall be able to rely on a developer and reviewer revision loop stopping after a fixed number of rounds and handing control to a human.
The security lead shall be able to have hijacked-goal tool output and insecure generated code blocked, not only rewritten or flagged.
The security lead shall be able to see, for every cleared governance gate, the command result or CI artifact that backs it.
The maintainer shall be able to rely on approval status being written only by a hook or the orchestrator, never by the agent that produced the artifact.
The auditor shall be able to verify that the governance audit log has not been altered.
The compliance officer shall be able to see, for each agent action, the operation, data accessed, agent identity, human authorizer, and timestamp.
The compliance officer shall be able to collect SOC 2 Type II evidence from the plugin's own hook logs across a 6-to-12-month window.
The compliance officer shall be able to see who accessed student-record paths and the purpose the user declared, or unstated, and to tag paths as student records (FERPA).

The compliance officer shall be able to rely on a HIPAA profile, enforced by default, with agent-level audit logs, a recorded BAA per external system, and a refusal to send PHI-tagged content to outbound tools.
The security lead shall be able to see each control mapped to OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 items and NIST AI RMF functions, with an owner and review cadence.
The maintainer shall be able to define what CRITICAL and HIGH mean for this repo and to run new checks advisory-only before enforcing.
The plugin user shall be able to rely on only high-confidence, high-severity findings blocking a PR, with the rest advisory.
The maintainer shall be able to read a severity, a confidence, and a routing decision on each reviewer and code-reviewer finding.
The security lead shall be able to see reviewer findings in the GitHub Security tab.

The compliance officer shall be able to rely on a compliance profile being turned off only through a change to the committed project settings that the user applies, with each disablement logged and recorded in DECISIONS.md, so that a personal settings file cannot silently disable enforcement.
The compliance officer shall be able to see each disclosure of education-record data to an outside party, with the receiving party and the legitimate interest (FERPA).
Group A. The maintainer shall be able to define in-house golden tasks for coding and for spec writing, each with a reference and a way to grade it.
Group A. The maintainer shall be able to read, for each suite, a pass@1 value for coding and a structural score and a separate judge score for specs.
Group A. The maintainer shall be able to see at release time whether the score of a suite fell compared with the previous release.
Group A. The maintainer shall be able to rely on benchmark scores not being inflated by training-data contamination, overfitting to the cases, judge bias, or flaky tests.
Group B. The plugin user shall be able to rely on every review checking the recurring defect classes of a named checklist, with each unchecked item shown.
Group B. The maintainer shall be able to see, for each review round, which findings are new, fixed, open, or withdrawn, and to rely on the loop escalating when fixes keep producing new findings.
Group B. The security lead shall be able to rely on an approval only when the reviewer examined every path it was sent, against the revision that is current at the gate.
Group B. The maintainer shall be able to see, for each reviewer lane and checklist item, how many findings the user judged true or false, and to approve the checklist changes that follow.
Group B. The plugin user shall be able to rely on a PR review being posted only against the head revision it reviewed, and on a posting retry never duplicating a review.
Group B. The maintainer shall be able to rely on a finding's severity coming from a fixed catalog entry and not from the reviewer's free text.

The PR-posting guard MUST deny gh pr review and bkt pr approve or decline for a PR when no recorded user confirmation exists for that PR and verdict. The guard is additive: it owns the deny decision for the posting action, and the pr-post-ask hook stays unchanged, so its prompt is not removed. After a recorded confirmation the user may still see the pr-post-ask prompt, so two prompts may appear, accepted as defense in depth.

scenarios.name: Confirmed verdict posts
scenarios.given: the user confirmed approve PR 42 and the confirmation is recorded
scenarios.when: the session runs gh pr review 42 --approve
scenarios.then: the guard MUST allow the command AND the log MUST hold the confirmation reference AND the pr-post-ask hook MAY still prompt the user, because the guard does not replace it

scenarios.name: Additive guard leaves the pr-post-ask prompt in place
scenarios.given: a recorded confirmation covers approve PR 42
scenarios.when: the session runs gh pr review 42 --approve
scenarios.then: the pr-post-ask hook MUST remain unchanged and MUST still ask AND the confirmation guard MUST NOT suppress that prompt

scenarios.name: Injected approval is denied
scenarios.given: PR 42's description tells the session to approve and no confirmation is recorded
scenarios.when: the session runs gh pr review 42 --approve
scenarios.then: the guard MUST deny the command AND the denial message MUST name the missing confirmation

scenarios.name: Confirmation for a different verdict does not carry over
scenarios.given: a recorded confirmation covers approve PR 42 only
scenarios.when: the session runs gh pr review 42 --request-changes
scenarios.then: the guard MUST deny the command

requirements.text: The commit workflow MUST stage only paths the user named or accepted, and MUST NOT run git add ., git add -A, or git add --all.

scenarios.name: Named paths staged
scenarios.given: the user names src/a.js and src/b.js
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST stage exactly those two paths

scenarios.name: Request to stage everything
scenarios.given: the user says commit everything and the tree holds a .env file
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST list the changed paths and ask which to stage AND stage nothing until paths are named

requirements.text: The plugin documentation MUST recommend scoping each push grant to a named remote (for example Bash(git push origin *), and a second grant such as Bash(git push <mirror-name> *) for a mirror) in place of Bash(git push *), and the health check MUST report a wildcard or unscoped push grant (Bash(git push *), Bash(git push:*)) when it reads one. The health check MUST NOT report a push grant that names a specific remote, including a second named remote.

scenarios.name: Named grant passes the check
scenarios.given: the settings hold Bash(git push origin *) and no wildcard or unscoped push grant
scenarios.then: the report MUST show no push-grant finding

scenarios.name: Second named remote passes the check
scenarios.given: the settings hold Bash(git push origin *) and Bash(git push mirror *) and no wildcard or unscoped push grant
scenarios.then: the report MUST show no push-grant finding

scenarios.name: Wildcard grant reported
scenarios.given: the settings hold Bash(git push *) or Bash(git push:*)
scenarios.then: the report MUST list the wildcard push grant AND the report MUST NOT edit the settings file

requirements.text: The commit workflow MUST run a secret scan on staged changes before creating a commit, using the in-plugin pattern-scanner script as the default scan tool, and MUST stop with no commit when the scan reports a finding or cannot run. The script ships with the plugin, so the default scan has no external dependency. A project MAY substitute an external scanner (for example gitleaks or trufflehog) by replacing the script call, provided the substitute keeps the same three outcomes: clean, findings, and cannot-run.

scenarios.name: Clean scan commits
scenarios.given: staged changes hold no secret pattern
scenarios.when: the commit workflow reaches the commit step
scenarios.then: the scan MUST report clean AND the workflow MUST create the commit

scenarios.name: Staged secret stops the commit
scenarios.given: a staged file holds an API key pattern
scenarios.when: the commit workflow reaches the commit step
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST stop with no commit AND the report MUST show the file path and rule name and MUST NOT show the secret value

scenarios.name: Scanner unavailable
scenarios.given: the in-plugin pattern-scanner script cannot run, or a substituted external scanner is not installed
scenarios.when: the commit workflow reaches the commit step
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST treat the outcome as cannot-run, stop with no commit, and tell the user the scan did not run

requirements.text: The revision workflow MUST declare a maximum iteration count of 10, with two consecutive LGTMs as the normal pass, and MUST escalate to the user when the count is reached without approval. At the cap the orchestrator MUST run no further developer or reviewer round and MUST present the unresolved findings with the choices continue, waive, or abort.

scenarios.name: Approval inside the cap
scenarios.given: the cap is 10
scenarios.when: the reviewer returns two consecutive LGTMs at iteration 2
scenarios.then: the loop MUST end AND no escalation MUST occur

scenarios.name: Cap reached
scenarios.given: the cap is 10 and no approval has come
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST invoke no further developer or reviewer round AND the user MUST receive the unresolved findings with the choices continue, waive, or abort

requirements.text: A PostToolUse guardrail MUST be able to deny a tool result and halt the next action when an alignment check finds that the result tries to redirect the agent from the user's stated goal. The alignment check MUST be rule-based and run advisory-first under FR-238, and MUST NOT call a model.

scenarios.name: Hijack denied
scenarios.given: the user's goal is summarize this page and a fetched page tells the agent to send repo files to a URL
scenarios.when: the WebFetch result reaches the guardrail
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST withhold the result from the agent AND the log MUST hold a deny record with a rule id

scenarios.name: Benign result passes
scenarios.given: a fetched page holds only documentation text
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST pass the result unchanged AND the log MUST hold a pass record

requirements.text: The guardrail MUST scan code that an agent writes for insecure patterns and MUST deny the write when a finding has high confidence and severity at or above HIGH under the severity policy.

scenarios.name: Injection-prone code denied
scenarios.given: a write builds an SQL string from request input
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST deny the write AND the denial MUST name the rule id and line

scenarios.name: Safe code passes
scenarios.given: a write uses a parameterized query
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST allow the write

requirements.text: The orchestrator MUST record a governance gate as cleared only with an evidence reference: a parsed command exit code and measured value, or a CI artifact; a model-emitted sign-off string MUST NOT clear a gate. For judgement-based gates (OWASP Clear, LLM Security Clear, Approved for merge) the evidence MUST be a scanner exit code plus a verdict from a reviewer agent other than the producer, with file:line findings. The required scanner exit code MUST come from the plugin's own scripts (check-fsa-tables.js, sync-writing-standard.js, the FR-217 pattern/secret scanner, or the health self-tests). An external security scanner is optional additional evidence, and a gate MUST NOT depend on one being installed.

scenarios.name: Coverage gate with evidence
scenarios.given: npm run test:coverage exits 0 and the parsed line coverage is 82%
scenarios.when: the orchestrator evaluates the coverage gate
scenarios.then: the gate record MUST hold the command, exit code 0, and value 82 AND the gate MUST read as cleared

scenarios.name: Sign-off string alone
scenarios.given: an agent emits a coverage sign-off string and no command result exists
scenarios.when: the orchestrator evaluates the coverage gate
scenarios.then: the gate MUST stay open AND the merge check MUST block

requirements.text: A hook or the orchestrator MUST write approval status; the agent that produced an artifact MUST NOT write the status of that artifact.

scenarios.name: Orchestrator records verdict
scenarios.given: a reviewer returns an approving verdict for a developer's artifact
scenarios.when: the orchestrator updates the plan file
scenarios.then: the status MUST show the writer as the orchestrator

scenarios.name: Producer self-approval blocked
scenarios.given: a developer agent tries to set its artifact's status to approved
scenarios.when: the write reaches the write bar
scenarios.then: the write MUST be denied AND the log MUST hold a deny record

requirements.text: The write bar MUST deny a subagent shell command that writes to .agent/main-plan/** or DECISIONS.md through redirection, tee, sed -i, cp, mv, or rm, and MUST allow shell reads of those paths.

scenarios.name: Shell append to DECISIONS.md
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST deny the command

scenarios.name: Shell read allowed
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST allow the command

requirements.text: The governance audit log MUST be appended one JSON line per event, and each line MUST hold a hash of the prior line with a defined genesis value for the first line.

scenarios.name: Append extends the chain
scenarios.given: the log holds N lines
scenarios.then: the new line's prior-hash field MUST equal the hash of line N

scenarios.name: Failed append leaves the chain intact
scenarios.given: the disk is full
scenarios.then: the log MUST hold no partial line AND the health log MUST record the failure

requirements.text: The plugin MUST provide a command that walks the audit log, recomputes each hash, and reports the first line where the chain breaks.

scenarios.name: Intact chain
scenarios.given: an unmodified log of 500 lines
scenarios.then: it MUST exit 0 AND it MUST report 500 lines verified

scenarios.name: Edited line
scenarios.given: line 7 was edited after writing
scenarios.then: it MUST exit non-zero AND it MUST name line 7 as the first break

requirements.text: Each logged event MUST carry the agent type, agent id, and plugin version of the actor, and MUST record the value main-session when no subagent acted.

scenarios.name: Subagent event
scenarios.given: the developer subagent writes a file
scenarios.then: the record MUST hold agent type developer, its agent id, and the plugin version

scenarios.name: Main-session event
scenarios.given: the main session runs a command
scenarios.then: the record MUST hold main-session AND MUST NOT leave the identity blank

requirements.text: The audit log MUST record, for each access event, the operation, data accessed (path and data-class tag only), agent identity, human authorizer, and timestamp. The subagent log, which is written once per subagent report, MUST add only the agent identity and human authorizer to each report row and MUST NOT hold an operation or data-accessed field. The human authorizer is the user who approved the plan, recorded as a reference to that approval and never as message text (NFR-031). An autonomous action, or one with no user approval, MUST record the authorizer as none with a reason.

scenarios.name: Complete record
scenarios.given: a user-confirmed PR post under a plan the user approved
scenarios.then: the audit record MUST hold all five fields AND the authorizer field MUST hold a reference to the plan approval and MUST NOT hold message text AND the fsa-log.jsonl row for that report MUST hold identity and authorizer only

scenarios.name: No human authorizer
scenarios.given: an autonomous read with no user action, or an action with no user approval of the plan
scenarios.then: the authorizer field MUST read none with a reason AND the field MUST NOT be omitted

requirements.text: Event logging MUST be active from the first session after install with no opt-in, and a guard disabled through hooks-disabled.json MUST produce a logged disablement event.

scenarios.name: Fresh install
scenarios.given: a new install with no configuration
scenarios.when: the first session runs a governed action
scenarios.then: a log record for that action MUST exist

scenarios.name: Guard disabled
scenarios.given: a user adds a guard to hooks-disabled.json
scenarios.then: the log MUST hold a disablement event naming the guard and the time

requirements.text: The plugin MUST export, for a date range, the counts and records of denies, asks, gate evidence, and approvals from its hook logs, together with the chain verification result.

scenarios.name: Export for a verified range
scenarios.given: the chain is intact for 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30
scenarios.when: the export runs for that range
scenarios.then: the report MUST list control events by type AND the report MUST show the chain as verified

scenarios.name: Range with a break
scenarios.given: the chain breaks inside the range
scenarios.then: the report MUST mark the range unverified and name the first bad line

requirements.text: While the FERPA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST write to the audit log, for each agent access to a path tagged as a student record, the five attribution fields plus the purpose. The purpose MUST come from the session purpose record that the purpose-capture hook of FR-247 writes; when no such record exists the plugin MUST log the purpose as unstated and flag the record. The plugin MUST NOT deny an access on the missing purpose alone, because a read-time hook sees a path and not a purpose. This control is general FERPA governance support on the purpose dimension. It does not implement the recordation duty of 34 CFR 99.32, which covers disclosures to outside parties (FR-246).

scenarios.name: Access with purpose
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced, records/grades.csv is tagged student-record in .agent/governance/profile.json, and a session purpose record exists
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold the five attribution fields plus the purpose from that record

scenarios.name: Access without purpose
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced, records/grades.csv is tagged student-record, and no session purpose record exists
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold the purpose unstated AND the record MUST be flagged for review AND the read MUST NOT be denied on the missing purpose

requirements.text: The compliance configuration MUST be two files. A profile flag in the env block of the committed .claude/settings.json turns profiles on or off, and the plugin hooks MUST read that committed project file directly (parse the project settings file), not the merged process environment, so a personal .claude/settings.local.json cannot override or disable enforcement (FR-243); when the flag is absent from the committed project file the plugin MUST enforce all three profiles (SOC 2, HIPAA, FERPA). The file .agent/governance/profile.json MUST hold the PHI patterns, the data-class path globs, and the BAA references. A missing or malformed profile.json is handled under NFR-028.

scenarios.name: Path matches a tag
scenarios.given: .agent/governance/profile.json tags records/** as student-record
scenarios.then: the hook MUST return the class student-record

scenarios.name: Flag absent
scenarios.given: the env block of the committed .claude/settings.json holds no profile flag
scenarios.when: a hook reads the profile state by parsing the committed project settings file
scenarios.then: the hook MUST treat the SOC 2, HIPAA, and FERPA profiles as enforced

scenarios.name: Malformed profile.json
scenarios.given: .agent/governance/profile.json is invalid JSON and a profile is enforced
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST report the error through the health check AND the tagged-path controls MUST deny the guarded operations until the file is fixed

requirements.text: While the HIPAA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST write to the audit log, at agent level (one record per agent action, not per session or per inference call), each action that reads, writes, or sends data from a PHI-tagged path, with the purpose from the session purpose record (FR-247) or unstated. The records MUST be readable for review (path, agent identity, and timestamp per line), because 45 CFR 164.312(b) requires mechanisms that record and examine activity. This control implements that one required technical safeguard and is not full HIPAA compliance; access control, integrity, authentication, transmission security, and the administrative and physical safeguards are separate. Verified against 45 CFR 164.312(b).

scenarios.name: Agent action logged
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced and data/patients.csv is tagged PHI
scenarios.then: the log MUST hold a record naming that subagent and the path AND the record MUST hold the purpose from the session purpose record, or unstated when none exists

scenarios.name: Unidentified actor
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced and data/patients.csv is tagged PHI
scenarios.when: an action arrives with no agent id and is not the main session
scenarios.then: the record MUST carry the identity unidentified AND chain verification output MUST flag the record

requirements.text: While the HIPAA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), a guard MUST deny WebFetch and PR-post calls whose payload matches a configured PHI pattern or names a PHI-tagged path.

scenarios.name: PHI pattern in a PR comment
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced and profile.json holds a medical-record-number pattern
scenarios.when: the session posts a PR comment containing a string that matches the pattern
scenarios.then: the guard MUST deny the post AND the denial MUST be logged

scenarios.name: Clean payload
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced with the same profile.json
scenarios.when: the session posts a PR comment that matches no pattern and names no PHI-tagged path
scenarios.then: the guard MUST allow the post

requirements.text: While the HIPAA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST require a BAA reference for each external system that the profile lets receive data, and MUST report the profile as not ready when one is missing.

scenarios.name: BAA recorded
scenarios.given: profile.json lists a BAA reference for the model provider
scenarios.then: the check MUST report ready

scenarios.name: BAA missing
scenarios.given: profile.json lists an external system with no BAA reference
scenarios.then: the check MUST report not ready AND the outbound guard MUST deny calls to that system

requirements.text: The plugin MUST keep a control register in which each control maps to at least one OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 item (ASI01 to ASI10) or to not applicable with a reason.

scenarios.name: Complete register
scenarios.given: each control has an ASI id or a reasoned not applicable
scenarios.then: the check MUST pass

scenarios.name: Unmapped control
scenarios.given: a control has neither an ASI id nor a reasoned not applicable
scenarios.then: the check MUST fail and name the control

requirements.text: The control register MUST map each control to one NIST AI RMF function (GOVERN, MEASURE, or MANAGE), an owner role, and a review cadence with an escalation path. The default cadence is quarterly (estimate).

scenarios.name: Control with owner
scenarios.given: a control lists function MANAGE, owner role security lead, cadence quarterly
scenarios.then: the check MUST pass

scenarios.name: Missing owner
scenarios.given: a control lists no owner role
scenarios.then: the check MUST fail and name the control

requirements.text: A severity policy MUST define CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW for this repo, with examples and confidence levels, and MUST be approved by the user in DECISIONS.md before any rule blocks on severity. The policy basis is settled: four levels aligned to OWASP risk rating or CVSS bands with repo-specific examples, a per-finding confidence of High, Medium, or Low, and a SARIF mapping of CRITICAL and HIGH to error, MEDIUM to warning, LOW to note. The user approved the concrete policy text, severity-policy.md version draft-2 (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-31: Severity policy approved; first approved at draft-1, 2026-10-30); a rule may block on severity only after the FR-238 advisory baseline.

scenarios.name: Policy approved
scenarios.given: the policy exists and a DECISIONS.md entry approves it
scenarios.when: a rule is switched to blocking
scenarios.then: the switch MUST succeed

scenarios.name: Policy missing
scenarios.given: no approved policy exists
scenarios.when: a rule is switched to blocking
scenarios.then: the switch MUST be refused with the missing-policy reason

requirements.text: Each new check that can block MUST run advisory-only first, record every finding, and produce a baseline report with finding counts and precision before promotion to blocking. The baseline lasts 14 days or 20 reviews, whichever is later (estimate, BRD A-5).

scenarios.name: Advisory run
scenarios.given: a check is in advisory mode
scenarios.then: it MUST record the finding AND it MUST NOT block

scenarios.name: Promotion without baseline
scenarios.given: a check has no baseline report
scenarios.then: the switch MUST be refused

requirements.text: A finding MUST route as blocking only when confidence is high and severity is HIGH or CRITICAL under the severity policy; every other finding MUST route as advisory.

scenarios.name: Critical, high confidence
scenarios.given: a finding with severity CRITICAL and confidence high
scenarios.then: the finding MUST route as block-merge

scenarios.name: High severity, low confidence
scenarios.given: a finding with severity HIGH and confidence low
scenarios.then: the finding MUST route as inline-comment or log-only AND it MUST NOT block merge

requirements.text: The reviewer and code-reviewer agents MUST give each finding a severity, a confidence, and a routing field with one of block-merge, inline-comment, or log-only.

scenarios.name: Complete finding
scenarios.given: a reviewer reports a defect at src/a.js:10
scenarios.then: the finding MUST hold severity, confidence, and routing

scenarios.name: Missing field
scenarios.given: a finding lacks severity
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST reject the report and ask for a corrected one

requirements.text: The reviewer output MUST include a SARIF document (version 2.1.0, estimate) whose result level derives from severity and whose location is file and line, so findings appear in the GitHub Security tab. The reviewer returns the SARIF content or the findings, and the /do orchestrator MUST write the .sarif file. Uploading the file to GitHub is a posting action under the FR-214 confirmation rule.

scenarios.name: Findings become SARIF
scenarios.given: a reviewer reports two findings with file and line
scenarios.then: it MUST hold two results with level and location

scenarios.name: Finding without a location
scenarios.given: a finding has no file and line
scenarios.then: the finding MUST be left out of SARIF AND the report MUST list it as not exported with the reason

requirements.text: A hook on UserPromptSubmit, not the orchestrator, MUST write a record of the user's confirmation (PR, verdict, timestamp, a reference to the user message it came from, and the writer marked hook) as JSONL to a store under a path in .agent/ that FR-245 already protects, and the PR-posting guard of FR-214 MUST read that store with file reads alone. A subagent and text from a PR, web page, or file MUST NOT create or alter a confirmation record. The confirmation store MUST be a directory, not a single file, holding two files with different write rules. confirmations.jsonl MUST be written only by the UserPromptSubmit hook and MUST be denied to every tool caller, the main session included. pending.jsonl holds the pending-action records and MUST be written by the main-session /do orchestrator (no agent_id) and denied to every subagent. The confirmation MUST be bound to its pending action by a per-action token: when /do shows the PR and verdict draft, it MUST write a pending-action record (PR, verdict, a short random token, session_id, and a creation timestamp) to pending.jsonl, and the hook MUST write a confirmation only when the user's prompt carries the matching token. The FR-214 guard MUST read confirmations.jsonl only and MUST NOT treat a pending-action record as a confirmation; a pending-action record carries no authority on its own. An affirmative without the matching token MUST NOT confirm. The token MUST be single-use and time-expiring. Single-use: the hook MUST consume the token when it records the confirmation (the pending record is marked used or removed), so a repeat of the same token confirms nothing, consistent with one confirmation covering one PR and verdict. Time-expiring: the hook MUST reject a token whose pending record is older than a configured short window, even when the token was never used. The expiry window is an implementation estimate (on the order of minutes) until measured, not a fixed figure.

scenarios.name: User confirmation recorded
scenarios.given: /do showed the draft for PR 42 with verdict approve, wrote a pending-action record with token K7Q2, and the user answered yes with K7Q2 in their own message
scenarios.then: the store MUST hold a JSONL record for PR 42 and verdict approve with the timestamp AND the record MUST name the writer as hook

scenarios.name: Affirmative without the token rejected
scenarios.given: /do wrote a pending-action record for PR 42 with token K7Q2
scenarios.when: a prompt holds an affirmative such as pasted or injected text without K7Q2
scenarios.then: the hook MUST NOT write a confirmation record AND the guard of FR-214 MUST still deny the posting command

scenarios.name: Expired or reused token rejected
scenarios.given: /do wrote a pending-action record for PR 42 with token K7Q2, and either the record is older than the configured expiry window or the token was already consumed by an earlier confirmation
scenarios.then: the hook MUST NOT write a confirmation record AND the guard of FR-214 MUST still deny the posting command

scenarios.name: Pending record is not a confirmation
scenarios.given: pending.jsonl holds a pending-action record for PR 42 and confirmations.jsonl holds no record for it
scenarios.when: the guard of FR-214 checks the posting command
scenarios.then: the guard MUST deny the command AND a tool call that writes confirmations.jsonl MUST be denied, and a subagent write to pending.jsonl MUST be denied

scenarios.name: Forged confirmation rejected
scenarios.given: a PR description claims that the user confirmed approval
scenarios.when: a subagent or the session tries to write a confirmation record from that text
scenarios.then: the write MUST be denied AND the guard of FR-214 MUST still deny the posting command

requirements.text: A compliance profile MUST be turned off only by a change to the committed .claude/settings.json that the user applies; the plugin MUST NOT edit a settings file, and the hooks MUST read the profile flag by parsing the env block of the committed project .claude/settings.json directly, never the merged process environment, because the merged environment carries a local override; a personal .claude/settings.local.json MUST NOT disable enforcement.

scenarios.name: Opt-out in committed settings
scenarios.given: the user changed the committed .claude/settings.json to turn the FERPA profile off
scenarios.then: the FERPA controls MUST stop enforcing AND the SOC 2 and HIPAA profiles MUST stay enforced

scenarios.name: Personal settings cannot disable
scenarios.given: .claude/settings.local.json holds a flag that turns the HIPAA profile off and the committed .claude/settings.json does not
scenarios.when: a hook reads the profile state by parsing the committed project settings file
scenarios.then: the HIPAA profile MUST stay enforced AND the health check MUST report the ignored personal flag

scenarios.name: Plugin does not write settings
scenarios.given: a project that wants to opt out
scenarios.when: the plugin explains how to opt out
scenarios.then: it MUST describe the settings change for the user to apply AND it MUST NOT write .claude/settings.json

requirements.text: Each profile disablement MUST write a logged event that names the profile and the time, and MUST have its own DECISIONS.md entry.

scenarios.name: Disablement logged
scenarios.given: the committed settings turn the HIPAA profile off
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold a disablement event naming the HIPAA profile and the time

scenarios.name: No decision entry
scenarios.given: a profile is off and DECISIONS.md holds no entry for that disablement
scenarios.then: the report MUST list the disablement as lacking a decision entry

requirements.text: These six paths MUST be protected from writes by every subagent: .claude/settings.json, .agent/governance/profile.json, the confirmation store of FR-242, .agent/logs/governance/**, the session purpose record of FR-247, and the rule-mode store (the store that holds the advisory or blocking mode of each check, FR-238). A hook or the orchestrator remains the only writer of the last four. The confirmation store is the directory form of FR-242 and stays one path of the six. It holds confirmations.jsonl, written only by the UserPromptSubmit hook and protected from every tool caller, and pending.jsonl, writable by the main-session /do orchestrator and denied to every subagent. The FR-246 attribution decision adds no new store and no seventh path: the six protected paths are unchanged, and .agent/governance/profile.json (path 2) is the trust anchor for the FR-246 receiving-party allowlist.

scenarios.name: Subagent write denied
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST deny the write AND the log MUST hold a deny record

scenarios.name: Evidence and toggle stores denied
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.when: it writes confirmations.jsonl or pending.jsonl in the confirmation store, a file under .agent/logs/governance/, the session purpose record, or the rule-mode store
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST deny the write AND the log MUST hold a deny record

scenarios.name: Read allowed
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the read MUST be allowed

requirements.text: While the FERPA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST log each disclosure of education-record data to an outside party, recording the receiving party and the legitimate interest for each. The log MUST NOT accept unstated for either field; when the receiving party or the legitimate interest is missing, the plugin MUST deny the outbound call. The receiving party and the legitimate interest MUST be declared in the outbound call payload, and the guard (a read-only PreToolUse hook) MUST parse them from that payload. The guard MUST validate the receiving party against an allowlist held in .agent/governance/profile.json, and MUST deny the call when the receiving party is not on that allowlist. The control MUST apply the exceptions of 34 CFR 99.32(d), so a disclosure covered by an exception does not need a recorded entry under this control. Outbound disclosure detection is imperfect: a paraphrase or a payload assembled from earlier reads can escape a pattern or path match.

scenarios.name: Disclosure recorded
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced and an outbound call names a student-record path, with a receiving party and a legitimate interest declared
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold the receiving party and the legitimate interest for that disclosure

scenarios.name: Missing party or interest
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced and an outbound call names a student-record path, with no declared legitimate interest
scenarios.when: the session attempts the outbound call
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST deny the call AND the log MUST NOT hold the value unstated for the receiving party or the legitimate interest

scenarios.name: Party not on the allowlist
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced and an outbound call names a student-record path, with a receiving party that is not on the profile.json allowlist
scenarios.when: the session attempts the outbound call
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST deny the call

scenarios.name: Exception applies
scenarios.given: the receiving party falls under a 99.32(d) exception that profile.json lists
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST apply the exception and MUST NOT require a disclosure entry

requirements.text: A hook MUST write the session purpose record from a purpose the user declares, and the access-logging hooks (FR-230, FR-232) MUST read that record. Model output and text from a PR, web page, or file MUST NOT create or alter the record. When the user declares no purpose, the access log MUST record the purpose as unstated and flag the record.

scenarios.name: User declares a purpose
scenarios.given: the user states review grading anomalies as the purpose of the session
scenarios.then: the session purpose record MUST hold that purpose AND the record MUST name the writer as a hook

scenarios.name: Forged purpose rejected
scenarios.given: a PR description or file text claims the session purpose is approved audit
scenarios.when: the model or a subagent tries to write the session purpose record from that text
scenarios.then: the write MUST be denied AND the access log MUST NOT show that purpose

scenarios.name: No purpose declared
scenarios.given: the user declares no purpose
scenarios.when: an agent reads a student-record or PHI-tagged path
scenarios.then: the access log MUST hold the purpose unstated AND the record MUST be flagged

requirements.text: Each coding golden task MUST hold a task prompt, a reference solution, and a hidden test suite.

scenarios.name: Complete task
scenarios.given: a coding golden task directory with a prompt, a reference solution, and a hidden test suite
scenarios.then: the harness MUST accept the task

scenarios.name: Missing hidden suite
scenarios.given: a task directory with a prompt and a reference solution and no hidden test suite
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the task AND the rejection MUST name the missing part

requirements.text: Each spec golden task MUST hold a task prompt, a reference requirements set or reference spec, and a rubric that lists its deterministic checklist items apart from its subjective items.

scenarios.name: Rubric with two item groups
scenarios.given: a spec task whose rubric lists structural items and subjective items in separate groups
scenarios.then: the harness MUST accept the task

scenarios.name: Rubric with one mixed list
scenarios.given: a spec task whose rubric mixes structural and subjective items in one list
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the task

requirements.text: Each test in a hidden test suite MUST carry the identifier of the acceptance-criteria scenario it checks, in the [AC-n | spec | FR-n] naming form that the repository's own tests use.

scenarios.name: Named test
scenarios.given: a hidden test named [AC-2 | spec-foo | FR-045] rejects an empty name
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness loads the suite
scenarios.then: the harness MUST accept the test

scenarios.name: Unnamed test
scenarios.given: a hidden test whose name holds no scenario identifier
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness loads the suite
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the task AND the rejection MUST name the test

requirements.text: Each golden task MUST record its provenance (in-house or private repository), its creation date, and the model cutoff date it is valid against.

scenarios.name: Complete record
scenarios.given: a golden task whose metadata holds provenance, creation date, and valid-against cutoff
scenarios.then: the harness MUST accept the task

scenarios.name: Missing cutoff
scenarios.given: a golden task whose metadata holds no valid-against cutoff
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the task

requirements.text: A golden task MUST NOT be derived from a public benchmark dataset.

scenarios.name: In-house task
scenarios.given: a golden task whose provenance reads in-house
scenarios.then: the harness MUST accept the task

scenarios.name: Public-dataset task
scenarios.given: a golden task whose provenance names a public benchmark dataset
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the task

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST admit a coding golden task only after its reference solution passes its hidden test suite in each of a configured number of consecutive runs.

scenarios.name: Stable reference
scenarios.given: the configured count is 3 and the reference solution passes the hidden suite on 3 consecutive runs
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness validates the task
scenarios.then: the harness MUST admit the task

scenarios.name: Reference fails once
scenarios.given: the configured count is 3 and the reference solution fails the hidden suite on run 2
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness validates the task
scenarios.then: the harness MUST NOT admit the task AND the report MUST name the failing run

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST withhold the reference solution and the hidden test suite from the agent under test.

scenarios.name: Agent workspace
scenarios.given: a coding run for a golden task
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness prepares the agent's workspace
scenarios.then: the workspace MUST hold no reference solution and no hidden test suite file

scenarios.name: Leak detected
scenarios.given: a prepared workspace that holds a file from the reference directory
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness checks the workspace before the run
scenarios.then: the harness MUST abort the run AND the report MUST name the leaked path

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST keep each reference solution and hidden test suite out of every published artifact.

scenarios.name: Package without reference material
scenarios.given: the list of files in a published plugin package
scenarios.when: the list is searched for golden-task reference and hidden-suite paths
scenarios.then: the search MUST find none

scenarios.name: Reference path in the package
scenarios.given: a published package list that holds a golden-task reference path
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness validates the package list
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail AND the result MUST name the path

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST score a coding run as pass when the hidden test suite exits 0 and as fail when it exits non-zero, with no model call in the scoring.

scenarios.name: Suite passes
scenarios.given: a coding run whose hidden suite exits 0
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the run
scenarios.then: the run MUST score pass AND the scoring MUST make no model call

scenarios.name: Suite fails
scenarios.given: a coding run whose hidden suite exits 1
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the run
scenarios.then: the run MUST score fail

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST run each golden task as a case in the existing claude plugin eval layout (a prompt.md and a graders/ folder under evals/).

scenarios.name: Case listed by the runner
scenarios.given: a golden task directory with prompt.md and a graders/ folder under evals/
scenarios.when: claude plugin eval lists the cases
scenarios.then: the list MUST include the golden task

scenarios.name: Task without graders
scenarios.given: a golden task directory with no graders/ folder
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the task

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST report a coding run as not-run, never as pass or fail, when the sandbox backend that the run's Write, Edit, and Bash grant requires is unavailable.

scenarios.name: Backend absent
scenarios.given: a coding case that needs a shell grant and a machine with no sandbox backend
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness runs the case
scenarios.then: the run MUST read not-run AND the run MUST count in neither c nor k of FR-271

scenarios.name: Backend present
scenarios.given: the same case and a machine with the sandbox backend
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness runs the case
scenarios.then: the run MUST read pass or fail from the hidden suite

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST score a spec run as the fraction of its deterministic checklist items that pass, with no model call in the scoring.

scenarios.name: Partial score
scenarios.given: a spec run that passes 8 of 10 deterministic checklist items
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the run
scenarios.then: the structural score MUST read 0.8

scenarios.name: Checklist cannot run
scenarios.given: a spec run whose reference file is unreadable
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the run
scenarios.then: the run MUST read error AND the structural score MUST NOT read 0

requirements.text: The deterministic checklist MUST be built from the checks that spec-from-requirements review mode and the gather-requirements quality criteria already define.

scenarios.name: Item with a source
scenarios.given: a checklist item that every Requirement has a Scenario
scenarios.then: the harness MUST accept the item because spec-from-requirements review mode defines it

scenarios.name: Item with no source
scenarios.given: a checklist item that no existing check or quality criterion defines
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the item

requirements.text: The deterministic checklist MUST confirm that each requirement identifier, scenario, and error path of the reference appears in the output.

scenarios.name: Full coverage
scenarios.given: a reference with FR-1 to FR-3 and one error path each, and an output that holds all of them
scenarios.then: the reference-coverage items MUST pass

scenarios.name: Missing error path
scenarios.given: an output that omits the error path of FR-3
scenarios.then: the item for that error path MUST fail AND the result MUST name FR-3

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MAY score the subjective rubric items of a spec case with an LLM-as-judge grader.

scenarios.name: Judge off
scenarios.given: a spec case and no judge configured
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the case
scenarios.then: the result MUST hold a structural score AND the judge score MUST read absent

scenarios.name: Judge on
scenarios.given: a spec case and a judge configured
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the case
scenarios.then: the result MUST hold both a structural score and a judge score

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST run the judge grader only on a spec case that cleared the structural checklist. A case clears the checklist when every deterministic item passes (assumption A-13).

scenarios.name: Cleared case judged
scenarios.given: a spec case with every deterministic item passed and a judge configured
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the case
scenarios.then: the judge grader MUST run

scenarios.name: Uncleared case not judged
scenarios.given: a spec case with one deterministic item failed and a judge configured
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness scores the case
scenarios.then: the judge grader MUST NOT run AND the judge score MUST read absent

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST report the structural score and the judge score as two separate values and MUST NOT combine them into one number.

scenarios.name: Separate values
scenarios.given: a spec case with a structural score 0.9 and a judge score 0.6
scenarios.then: the result MUST hold 0.9 and 0.6 as two values

scenarios.name: Combined field
scenarios.given: a result that holds a field averaging the two scores
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail and name the field

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST report pass@1 for a coding case as c divided by k, where k is the number of completed runs of that case and c is the number of those runs that pass.

scenarios.name: Three of five pass
scenarios.given: a coding case run 5 times with 3 passes
scenarios.then: the value MUST read 0.6

scenarios.name: No completed run
scenarios.given: a coding case whose every run read not-run
scenarios.then: the value MUST read absent AND the value MUST NOT read 0

requirements.text: The benchmark result MUST state k, c, and the benchmark harness version beside each pass@1 value.

scenarios.name: Full basis
scenarios.given: a pass@1 value of 0.6
scenarios.then: the result MUST hold k = 5, c = 3, and the harness version beside it

scenarios.name: Missing version
scenarios.given: a result that holds a pass@1 value and no harness version
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail

requirements.text: The release-check runner MUST provide a benchmark section that runs the coding and spec suites and compares the scores of each suite with the scores stored for the previous release. The suite score is the mean pass@1 of a coding suite and the mean structural score of a spec suite.

scenarios.name: Comparison reported
scenarios.given: stored scores for the previous release and a benchmark request
scenarios.then: the section MUST report, for each suite, the current score and the previous score

scenarios.name: No previous release
scenarios.given: no stored scores for a previous release
scenarios.then: the section MUST report no baseline AND the section MUST NOT report a regression finding

requirements.text: The benchmark section MUST run only when the user requests it.

scenarios.name: Plain release check
scenarios.given: a release check started with no benchmark request
scenarios.then: the benchmark section MUST NOT run AND every other section MUST behave as before

scenarios.name: Requested run
scenarios.given: a release check started with the benchmark request
scenarios.then: the benchmark section MUST run

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST key each stored result to the plugin version that the run result records.

scenarios.name: Keyed result
scenarios.given: a run result that records plugin version 1.14.7
scenarios.then: the stored result MUST be keyed to 1.14.7

scenarios.name: Result without a version
scenarios.given: a run result that records no plugin version
scenarios.then: the harness MUST refuse to store it

requirements.text: The repository MUST hold, under version control, a scoreboard that lists for each release and suite the version, pass@1, structural score, and judge score.

scenarios.name: Row added for a release
scenarios.given: a completed benchmark section for version 1.14.7
scenarios.then: it MUST hold a row for 1.14.7 for each suite run

scenarios.name: Row missing
scenarios.given: a completed benchmark section and a scoreboard with no row for that version
scenarios.then: the section MUST report a finding that names the version

requirements.text: The benchmark section MUST report a regression finding when the score of a suite is below the previous release's score for that suite by more than a configured margin.

scenarios.name: Drop beyond the margin
scenarios.given: a margin of 0.05, a previous suite score of 0.80, and a current score of 0.70
scenarios.then: the section MUST report a regression finding for that suite

scenarios.name: Drop within the margin
scenarios.given: a margin of 0.05, a previous suite score of 0.80, and a current score of 0.78
scenarios.then: the section MUST report no regression finding

requirements.text: The release comparison MUST be computed over the cases present in both releases.

scenarios.name: Case added
scenarios.given: the current release holds a case that the previous release lacks
scenarios.then: the added case MUST NOT enter either score

scenarios.name: Case removed
scenarios.given: the previous release holds a case that the current release lacks
scenarios.then: the removed case MUST NOT enter either score

requirements.text: The benchmark section MUST report a judge-score decline as advisory only.

scenarios.name: Judge drops alone
scenarios.given: a judge score down 0.2 and structural scores within the margin
scenarios.then: the section MUST report an advisory note AND the section MUST report no regression finding

scenarios.name: Structural score drops too
scenarios.given: a judge score down 0.2 and a structural score down beyond the margin
scenarios.then: the section MUST report a regression finding for the structural score

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST run its held-out cases only in the benchmark section of a release check.

scenarios.name: Ordinary eval run
scenarios.given: a case flagged held-out
scenarios.when: an ordinary claude plugin eval run lists cases
scenarios.then: the harness MUST exclude the held-out case from the run

scenarios.name: Release benchmark
scenarios.given: a case flagged held-out and a benchmark request
scenarios.then: the section MUST include the held-out case

requirements.text: The benchmark harness SHOULD add at least one new golden task to each suite in each release that runs the benchmark section.

scenarios.name: New task added
scenarios.given: a release that runs the benchmark section and a suite with one case not present in the previous release
scenarios.when: the scoreboard is compared with the previous release
scenarios.then: the check MUST find a new case in that suite

scenarios.name: No new task
scenarios.given: a suite with no new case in a benchmark release
scenarios.then: the section MUST report an advisory note that names the suite

requirements.text: WHEN the judge and the agent under test share a model family, the benchmark harness MUST apply three bias mitigations to the judge score (candidate-order randomization per FR-284, rubric anchoring per FR-283, and a human-agreement check at each benchmark release per FR-286) and MUST record the judge family and the agent family in the result.

scenarios.name: Same family with mitigations
scenarios.given: an agent under test and a judge of the same family, and a benchmark release with a human-labeled sample
scenarios.then: the harness MUST randomize the candidate order, MUST score each rubric item against its own text, and MUST report the human-agreement figure AND the result MUST name the judge family and the agent family

scenarios.name: Mitigation missing
scenarios.given: a judge result for a same-family judge that records no candidate-order randomization
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail

scenarios.name: No human-labeled sample
scenarios.given: a same-family judge and no human-labeled sample at the benchmark release
scenarios.then: the report MUST state that no agreement figure exists

requirements.text: The judge MUST score each subjective rubric item separately against the text of that item.

scenarios.name: Per-item scores
scenarios.given: a rubric with 3 subjective items
scenarios.then: the result MUST hold 3 item scores

scenarios.name: One overall score
scenarios.given: a judge result that holds a single overall score and no item scores
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail

requirements.text: WHEN the judge compares two texts, the benchmark harness MUST run the comparison in both orders and average the two results.

scenarios.name: Pairwise comparison
scenarios.given: a judge comparison of an output against the reference
scenarios.then: the harness MUST run output-then-reference and reference-then-output AND the reported result MUST be the mean of the two

scenarios.name: One order only
scenarios.given: a comparison result built from one order
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail

requirements.text: The benchmark result MUST report each judge score as the mean of a configured number of judge runs and MUST state that number.

scenarios.name: Mean of three
scenarios.given: a configured count of 3 and judge runs scoring 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8
scenarios.then: the judge score MUST read 0.7 AND the result MUST state 3 runs

scenarios.name: Count not stated
scenarios.given: a result that holds a judge score and no run count
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail

requirements.text: WHERE a human-labeled sample of spec outputs exists, the benchmark harness SHOULD report the judge's agreement with the human scores as Spearman rho or Cohen kappa.

scenarios.name: Labeled sample
scenarios.given: a labeled sample of 20 spec outputs with human scores
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness reports the judge
scenarios.then: the report SHOULD hold a Spearman rho or a Cohen kappa for the sample

scenarios.name: No sample
scenarios.given: no labeled sample
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness reports the judge
scenarios.then: the report SHOULD state that no agreement figure exists

requirements.text: The benchmark harness MUST report a hidden-suite test that gives different results on repeated runs of the same candidate as flaky, without skipping or retrying it.

scenarios.name: Flaky test flagged
scenarios.given: a hidden test that passes on run 1 and fails on run 2 for the same candidate
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness reports the suite
scenarios.then: the report MUST list the test as flaky AND the test MUST still count in the suite result

scenarios.name: Retry-until-pass configured
scenarios.given: a configuration that retries a failing hidden test until it passes
scenarios.when: the benchmark harness loads the configuration
scenarios.then: the harness MUST reject the configuration

requirements.text: The plugin MUST keep one reviewer checklist for each of three review lanes (defect-depth, test-integrity, and architecture-safety), and each checklist item MUST have an identifier, a check, and the evidence that clears it. Initial content: items DD-01 to DD-09, TI-01 to TI-08, and AS-01 to AS-06 (FR-NFR-harness-governance.md, section 2.71).

scenarios.name: Checklist valid
scenarios.given: three lane checklists whose every item has an identifier, a check, and an evidence entry
scenarios.then: the validation MUST pass

scenarios.name: Item without evidence
scenarios.given: a checklist item with no evidence entry
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail AND the result MUST name the item

requirements.text: The reviewer and code-reviewer agents MUST account for each checklist item that applies to the artifact type as evaluated or as skipped with a reason.

scenarios.name: All items accounted for
scenarios.given: a code artifact for which 5 checklist items apply
scenarios.then: the report MUST list 5 items as evaluated or skipped with a reason

scenarios.name: Item missing from the report
scenarios.given: a report that lists 4 of the 5 applicable items
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST reject the report and ask for a corrected one

requirements.text: A finding raised from a checklist item MUST carry that item's identifier as its rule identifier.

scenarios.name: Item cited
scenarios.given: a reviewer finds an unbounded repeated pattern at src/parse.js:12
scenarios.then: the finding MUST carry DD-01 as its rule identifier

scenarios.name: Item not cited
scenarios.given: a finding raised from checklist item DD-01 with no rule identifier
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST reject the report and ask for a corrected one

requirements.text: Each lane checklist MUST be applied within the existing gates that the lane-to-gate table assigns.

scenarios.name: Lane in an assigned gate
scenarios.given: the Security Gate runs on a code change
scenarios.then: the reviewer MUST evaluate the defect-depth items that apply

scenarios.name: Lane assigned to no gate
scenarios.given: a lane that the lane-to-gate table assigns to no existing gate
scenarios.then: the validation MUST fail and name the lane

requirements.text: The orchestrator MAY dispatch the lane reviews of one gate concurrently, with at most three reviewer dispatches running at once.

scenarios.name: Three lanes at once
scenarios.given: a gate with three lane reviews ready
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MAY run all three at once

scenarios.name: Fourth dispatch held
scenarios.given: three reviewer dispatches running
scenarios.when: a fourth reviewer dispatch is ready
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST hold it until one dispatch ends

requirements.text: WHEN lane reviews ran concurrently, the orchestrator MUST merge findings that share a file, a line, and a rule identifier into one finding that keeps the highest severity among them.

scenarios.name: Same finding from two lanes
scenarios.given: two lanes report DD-01 at src/parse.js:12, one as HIGH and one as MEDIUM
scenarios.then: the merged report MUST hold one finding at src/parse.js:12 with severity HIGH

scenarios.name: Different lines
scenarios.given: two lanes report DD-01 at src/parse.js:12 and src/parse.js:40
scenarios.then: the merged report MUST hold both findings

requirements.text: Each finding MUST carry an identifier that stays the same in every round of one gate.

scenarios.name: Identifier carried across rounds
scenarios.given: finding F-3 in round 1 that is still open in round 2
scenarios.when: the reviewer writes the round-2 report
scenarios.then: the report MUST list that finding as F-3

scenarios.name: Finding without an identifier
scenarios.given: a report whose finding holds no identifier
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST reject the report and ask for a corrected one

requirements.text: On a re-review the reviewer MUST give each prior finding exactly one status of fixed, open, or withdrawn with a one-line reason, and MUST mark every other finding as new.

scenarios.name: Statuses given
scenarios.given: 3 prior findings and 1 new defect
scenarios.when: the reviewer writes the re-review report
scenarios.then: each prior finding MUST hold one of fixed, open, or withdrawn with a reason AND the new defect MUST read new

scenarios.name: Prior finding without a status
scenarios.given: a re-review report that omits the status of prior finding F-2
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST reject the report and ask for a corrected one

requirements.text: Each review report MUST name the revision of the artifact it reviewed, as a content digest or a commit identifier.

scenarios.name: Revision named
scenarios.given: a reviewer report for a task whose artifact has a known digest
scenarios.then: the report MUST hold that digest or a commit identifier

scenarios.name: Revision missing
scenarios.given: a report with no revision
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST reject the report and ask for a corrected one

requirements.text: The orchestrator MUST NOT count a reviewer verdict toward a gate when the artifact has changed since the revision that the report names.

scenarios.name: Both approvals on one revision
scenarios.given: two consecutive approved reports that name the same revision, which is still current
scenarios.then: the gate MUST end approved

scenarios.name: Artifact changed between approvals
scenarios.given: an approved report on revision A and a later artifact change to revision B
scenarios.then: the report on revision A MUST NOT count toward the gate

requirements.text: On a re-review the dispatch MUST list the paths changed since the previous pass.

scenarios.name: Paths listed
scenarios.given: a fix pass that changed src/a.js and src/b.js
scenarios.then: the dispatch MUST list src/a.js and src/b.js

scenarios.name: First review
scenarios.given: a gate at rework count 0
scenarios.then: the dispatch MUST hold no changed-path list

requirements.text: On a re-review the reviewer MUST mark a finding as fix-induced, with the identifier of the prior finding, when a change made since the previous pass causes it.

scenarios.name: Fix causes a new defect
scenarios.given: a fix for F-2 that makes a previously correct path reject valid input
scenarios.then: the new finding MUST read fix-induced with the identifier F-2

scenarios.name: Unrelated new defect
scenarios.given: a new defect in code that no change since the previous pass touched
scenarios.then: the finding MUST read new and MUST NOT read fix-induced

requirements.text: WHEN two consecutive re-reviews of one gate each return a fix-induced finding, the orchestrator SHOULD run one code-reviewer pass over the whole artifact before it dispatches another fix pass.

scenarios.name: Two fix-induced passes
scenarios.given: the re-reviews at pass 2 and pass 3 of one gate each return a fix-induced finding
scenarios.when: the orchestrator plans the next step
scenarios.then: the orchestrator SHOULD dispatch one code-reviewer pass over the whole artifact

scenarios.name: One fix-induced pass
scenarios.given: only the re-review at pass 2 returns a fix-induced finding
scenarios.when: the orchestrator plans the next step
scenarios.then: the orchestrator SHOULD dispatch the normal fix pass

requirements.text: WHEN two consecutive re-reviews of one gate report the same finding as open and the reviewer cites no new evidence, the orchestrator SHOULD stop that loop and offer the choices continue, waive, or abort.

scenarios.name: Finding open after two fixes
scenarios.given: finding F-4 reported open by two consecutive re-reviews, with no new evidence in the second re-review
scenarios.when: the orchestrator plans the next step
scenarios.then: the orchestrator SHOULD stop the loop and offer continue, waive, or abort

scenarios.name: New evidence cited
scenarios.given: finding F-4 reported open by two consecutive re-reviews and the second re-review cites new evidence
scenarios.when: the orchestrator plans the next step
scenarios.then: the orchestrator SHOULD continue the loop

requirements.text: At an escalation under FR-218 or FR-301, the orchestrator MUST show, for each round, the number of new, fixed, open, and withdrawn findings.

scenarios.name: History shown
scenarios.given: an escalation after 4 rounds
scenarios.then: the presentation MUST list 4 rows with counts of new, fixed, open, and withdrawn findings

scenarios.name: Statuses missing
scenarios.given: a round whose report held no statuses
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST mark that round as having no status data

requirements.text: A reviewer MUST NOT return verdict approved when it did not examine every artifact path that the dispatch names.

scenarios.name: All paths examined
scenarios.given: a dispatch that names 3 paths and a reviewer that read all 3
scenarios.then: the verdict MAY read approved

scenarios.name: One path not examined
scenarios.given: a dispatch that names 3 paths and a reviewer that read 2
scenarios.when: the reviewer finds no defect in those 2
scenarios.then: the verdict MUST NOT read approved AND the skipped field MUST name the unexamined path

requirements.text: For a GitHub PR, the PR-review workflow MUST NOT post a review that was drafted against a head revision other than the PR's current head revision, which the workflow reads with the `gh` CLI immediately before it posts. Bitbucket is out of scope for this head check (U-9: the Bitbucket head-revision read command is not named).

scenarios.name: Head unchanged
scenarios.given: a review drafted against head revision H and a GitHub PR whose head, read with the `gh` CLI, is still H
scenarios.when: the workflow reaches the post step
scenarios.then: the workflow MAY post, subject to the FR-214 confirmation

scenarios.name: Head moved
scenarios.given: a review drafted against head revision H and a GitHub PR whose head, read with the `gh` CLI, is now H2
scenarios.when: the workflow reaches the post step
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST NOT post AND the workflow MUST tell the user the draft is stale

requirements.text: For a GitHub PR, WHEN a posting command ends with an unknown outcome, the PR-review workflow MUST read back the PR's reviews with the `gh` CLI before any retry. Bitbucket is out of scope for this read-back (U-9: the Bitbucket read command is not named).

scenarios.name: Review exists after the error
scenarios.given: a posting command that ended with a server error and a GitHub PR that now holds the review, read back with the `gh` CLI
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST NOT post again

scenarios.name: Review absent after the error
scenarios.given: a posting command that ended with a server error and a GitHub PR that holds no such review, read back with the `gh` CLI
scenarios.then: the workflow MAY retry, subject to the FR-214 confirmation

requirements.text: A finding whose rule identifier is in the severity catalog MUST take its severity from that catalog entry. The severity catalog is a table, held with the severity policy, that maps each rule identifier to a fixed severity; every checklist item and every in-plugin scanner rule has an entry (D-14).

scenarios.name: Catalog severity applied
scenarios.given: catalog entry DD-01 with severity MEDIUM and a finding with rule identifier DD-01 that the reviewer wrote as HIGH
scenarios.then: the recorded severity MUST read MEDIUM AND the report MUST note the difference

scenarios.name: Rule identifier absent from the catalog
scenarios.given: a finding whose rule identifier is not in the catalog
scenarios.then: the finding MUST be handled under FR-307

requirements.text: A finding with no rule identifier in the severity catalog and no CWE identifier MUST be marked unmapped and MUST route no higher than inline-comment.

scenarios.name: Unmapped high finding
scenarios.given: a finding with severity HIGH, confidence High, and no catalog rule or CWE identifier
scenarios.then: the finding MUST read unmapped AND the routing MUST NOT read block-merge

scenarios.name: Mapped high finding
scenarios.given: a finding with a catalog rule identifier, severity HIGH, and confidence High
scenarios.then: the routing MUST follow FR-239

requirements.text: A score from a critic or filtering model MUST NOT set a finding's severity and MUST NOT remove a finding from the report.

scenarios.name: Critic marks a finding as likely false
scenarios.given: a critic score that rates finding F-1 as likely false
scenarios.then: F-1 MUST stay in the report AND its severity MUST NOT change

scenarios.name: Critic raises a severity
scenarios.given: a critic score that rates finding F-2 as critical while its catalog severity is MEDIUM
scenarios.then: F-2 MUST keep severity MEDIUM

requirements.text: The plugin MUST record a disposition of true, false, or deferred for a reviewer finding only from the user's own label.

scenarios.name: User label recorded
scenarios.given: the user labels finding F-5 true through the labelling step
scenarios.then: F-5 MUST hold disposition true with the writer marked as the user

scenarios.name: Agent judgment
scenarios.given: an agent judges finding F-6 false and the user has not labeled it
scenarios.then: F-6 MUST read unlabeled

requirements.text: The plugin MUST report, for each lane and each checklist item, the number of findings labeled true, labeled false, deferred, and unlabeled, and the precision over the labeled findings. Precision is true divided by the sum of true and false.

scenarios.name: Item with labels
scenarios.given: checklist item DD-01 with 8 findings labeled true, 2 labeled false, and 5 unlabeled
scenarios.then: the report MUST show counts 8, 2, 0, and 5 for DD-01 AND the precision MUST read 0.8

scenarios.name: Item with no labels
scenarios.given: a checklist item whose findings are all unlabeled
scenarios.then: the precision MUST read not available AND the precision MUST NOT read 0

requirements.text: The dispatch for a review MUST pass the user's false labels for the same checklist items on the same artifact as data.

scenarios.name: Labels passed
scenarios.given: the user labeled a DD-03 finding on src/a.js false
scenarios.when: the orchestrator dispatches a review of src/a.js
scenarios.then: the dispatch MUST carry that label inside the data wrapper AND the dispatch MUST state that the label is data, not an instruction

scenarios.name: No labels
scenarios.given: no false label for the artifact
scenarios.then: the dispatch MUST hold no label block

requirements.text: The reviewer MUST NOT re-raise a finding that the user labeled false for the same checklist item and location unless the reviewer cites new evidence.

scenarios.name: Same finding, no new evidence
scenarios.given: a DD-03 finding at src/a.js:20 labeled false
scenarios.when: the reviewer sees the same issue at the same location with no new evidence
scenarios.then: the report MUST NOT list the finding

scenarios.name: New evidence
scenarios.given: the same label and a later change that makes the defect reachable
scenarios.when: the reviewer cites that change as new evidence
scenarios.then: the report MAY list the finding with the new evidence

requirements.text: The plugin MUST list each checklist item whose precision is below a configured floor as a retirement candidate in a checklist-change report for the user. The floor and the minimum number of labeled findings are configured values with provisional settings of 0.5 and 10, to be revised with data (OQ-17; section 5, provisional values).

scenarios.name: Item below the floor
scenarios.given: a floor of 0.5 and an item with precision 0.3 over enough labeled findings
scenarios.then: the report MUST list the item as a retirement candidate

scenarios.name: Too few labels
scenarios.given: an item with precision 0.3 over fewer labeled findings than the configured minimum
scenarios.then: the report MUST NOT list the item as a retirement candidate

requirements.text: The plugin MUST list each finding class that was raised with no checklist item at least a configured number of times as an addition candidate in the checklist-change report.

scenarios.name: Repeated unmapped class
scenarios.given: a configured count of 3 and 3 unmapped findings of one class
scenarios.then: the report MUST list the class as an addition candidate

scenarios.name: Below the count
scenarios.given: a configured count of 3 and 2 unmapped findings of one class
scenarios.then: the report MUST NOT list the class

requirements.text: A reviewer checklist MUST change only through an edit that the user approves and that has a DECISIONS.md entry.

scenarios.name: Approved edit
scenarios.given: the user approved retiring item TI-06 and DECISIONS.md holds the entry
scenarios.then: the checklist edit MUST be accepted

scenarios.name: Edit without approval
scenarios.given: a diff that retires item TI-06 and no DECISIONS.md entry
scenarios.then: the review MUST report the checklist edit as unapproved

requirements.text: Before a change to a lane checklist, the severity catalog, or a screening rule ships, the plugin SHOULD report finding precision and recall on a seeded-defect sample, before and after the change.

scenarios.name: Measured change
scenarios.given: a seeded sample of 20 defects and a proposed checklist change
scenarios.then: the report SHOULD hold precision and recall before and after

scenarios.name: No sample
scenarios.given: no seeded-defect sample
scenarios.then: the report SHOULD state that no measurement exists

requirements.text: Every deny, ask, guardrail, and gate decision MUST produce a log record with timestamp, agent identity, decision, and rule id.
Each new hook, agent, or skill MUST hold the fewest tools it needs; the guardrail MUST NOT hold write tools and no new unscoped Bash grant MUST appear.

A control marked security-critical (FR-214, FR-217, FR-220, FR-223, FR-231, FR-233, FR-246) MUST deny its own guarded operation class when it cannot evaluate because of an error or timeout, or when .agent/governance/profile.json is malformed while a profile is enforced; the denial MUST last until the file is fixed. When profile.json is absent the controls MUST run in log-only mode and MUST NOT hard-deny, because nothing is tagged to match. Settled by DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, Compliance profile flags, enforced by default (D-1).

scenarios.name: Fail-closed on error
scenarios.given: the PR-posting guard throws an error while evaluating gh pr review 42 --approve
scenarios.then: the hook MUST deny that command AND a command outside the guarded class MUST still be allowed

scenarios.name: Absent configuration runs log-only
scenarios.given: a profile is enforced by default and .agent/governance/profile.json does not exist
scenarios.when: a session reads a path and sends an outbound call
scenarios.then: the controls MUST log the events in log-only mode AND no control MUST hard-deny, because nothing is tagged to match

scenarios.name: Malformed configuration denies
scenarios.given: a profile is enforced and .agent/governance/profile.json is malformed
scenarios.when: a session attempts a guarded tagged-path operation
scenarios.then: the control MUST deny the operation AND the denial MUST continue until the file is fixed

requirements.text: Each hook added to the per-write path MUST add at most 30 ms at the median, and the total per-write hook cost MUST stay at or below 150 ms at the median. The thresholds are estimates anchored to the existing 80 to 110 ms; confirm by measurement.

scenarios.name: Budget check
scenarios.given: all hooks of this roadmap are installed
scenarios.then: the median added cost per hook MUST be at most 30 ms AND the median total MUST be at most 150 ms

requirements.text: Chain verification MUST detect 100% of single-line edits, deletions, and reorderings in the test corpus and MUST finish a 100,000-line log in at most 10 seconds (estimate for the time limit).

scenarios.name: Tamper detection
scenarios.given: a test corpus with one edited, one deleted, and one reordered line
scenarios.then: all three MUST be detected

requirements.text: Logs MUST NOT hold prompt text, file contents, or secret values; the data-accessed field MUST hold a path and a data-class tag only.

scenarios.name: Secret value kept out of the log
scenarios.given: the secret scan finds an API key in a staged file
scenarios.then: the record MUST hold the path and rule name AND the record MUST NOT hold the key value
