requirements.text: Audit and subagent logs MUST rotate by size, each new segment MUST carry the prior segment's final chain hash so the hash chain verifies across the cut, and segments MUST be retained for at least 12 months. The rotation size is an estimate until measured against NFR-030.

scenarios.name: Rotation keeps the chain
scenarios.given: the log reaches its configured rotation size (an estimate until measured)
scenarios.then: the first line of the new segment MUST hold the hash of the last line of the old segment AND chain verification MUST pass across the cut

requirements.text: A compliance control that rests on a vendor blog or an unverified citation MUST be labeled directional, and a control MUST NOT be marked complete before verification against the regulation text. Status: the HIPAA audit control (FR-232) is verified against 45 CFR 164.312(b), which requires mechanisms that record and examine activity, and the control implements that one required technical safeguard, not full HIPAA compliance. The FERPA internal access log (FR-230) carries no 34 CFR 99.32 citation and is general governance support, labeled directional. The FERPA disclosure-recordation control (FR-246) is the only control cited against 34 CFR 99.32; it stays to verify until its exception handling is reviewed. The exact log rotation size of NFR-032 is an estimate until measured against the NFR-030 verification-time target. The severity-policy basis (FR-237) is settled and the user approved the concrete policy text, severity-policy.md version draft-2 (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-31: Severity policy approved; first approved at draft-1, 2026-10-30); a rule may block on severity only after the FR-238 advisory baseline. The figures "under 50% mitigation" and "18% governance councils" MUST NOT serve as a threshold.

scenarios.name: Unverified FERPA disclosure control
scenarios.given: the FERPA disclosure-recordation control (FR-246) has no verification note
scenarios.then: the control status MUST read to verify and not complete

scenarios.name: FERPA internal log not cited as 99.32
scenarios.given: the FERPA internal access log (FR-230) sits in the control register
scenarios.then: the entry MUST NOT cite 34 CFR 99.32 and MUST read as general governance support

scenarios.name: HIPAA control states its scope
scenarios.given: the HIPAA audit control (FR-232) is marked verified
scenarios.then: the entry MUST cite 45 CFR 164.312(b) as one safeguard AND the entry MUST NOT claim full HIPAA compliance

requirements.text: A rule MUST NOT move from advisory to blocking unless its baseline precision is at least 90% (estimate, BRD A-6). The user labels each baseline advisory finding true or false, and the baseline report computes precision from those user-set labels, not from an agent's self-judgment.

scenarios.name: Low-precision promotion
scenarios.given: a baseline precision of 70%, computed from the user's true or false labels on the baseline findings
scenarios.when: the rule is switched to blocking
scenarios.then: the switch MUST be refused with the precision value

scenarios.name: Agent self-judgment does not set precision
scenarios.given: a baseline finding has no user label and an agent judges it true
scenarios.then: the report MUST NOT count the agent's judgment as a label AND the report MUST show the finding as unlabelled

requirements.text: Each new guard or filter MUST ship a self-test corpus with a known-safe and a known-prohibited case, report through the health check, and pass the table sync checks.
Every change to the LLM surface made for this roadmap MUST carry LLM Security Clear before merge, and any write-guard narrowing MUST follow a DECISIONS.md entry.
Scoring the same spec output with the deterministic checklist MUST give an identical structural score on every repetition.

scenarios.name: Repeated scoring
scenarios.given: one spec output and the deterministic checklist
scenarios.then: all 10 structural scores MUST be equal

requirements.text: Each benchmark run result MUST record its total model cost in USD and its elapsed time. Context (estimates, not a guaranteed budget): the single source run recorded in the research report, 8 cases, took about 165 seconds and about 4.85 USD; a full run of 10 coding and 10 spec cases at 5 runs each is estimated at 25 to 75 USD, not measured on this repository.

scenarios.name: Cost recorded
scenarios.given: a completed benchmark run
scenarios.then: the result MUST hold a total cost and an elapsed time

requirements.text: The scoreboard and the benchmark logs MUST hold scores, identifiers, and versions only, and MUST NOT hold reference solutions, hidden-suite text, or agent output text.

scenarios.name: Scoreboard content
scenarios.given: a scoreboard row for a release
scenarios.then: it MUST hold the version, suite, and scores only AND it MUST NOT hold hidden-suite text

requirements.text: A capability of Group B MUST NOT add a write or shell tool to reviewer or code-reviewer, whose tools MUST stay Read, Grep, Glob, LSP.

scenarios.name: Reviewer tools unchanged
scenarios.given: the reviewer and code-reviewer agent files after a Group B change
scenarios.then: each MUST list only Read, Grep, Glob, LSP

requirements.text: The gate outcome MUST record the number of reviewer dispatches used, so the extra cost of concurrent lane review is measurable. Concurrent lanes cost about three times one pass (estimate, to confirm by measurement).

scenarios.name: Dispatch count recorded
scenarios.given: a gate that ran three lane reviews
scenarios.then: it MUST state 3 reviewer dispatches

requirements.text: The disposition and finding records MUST hold identifiers, locations, rule identifiers, severity, confidence, and the user's label only, and MUST NOT hold file contents, secret values, or matched text.

scenarios.name: Record content
scenarios.given: a finding whose text quotes a secret value from the reviewed file
scenarios.then: the record MUST hold the path, line, and rule identifier AND the record MUST NOT hold the secret value

open_questions: OQ-1: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Judgement-gate evidence and the /do human authorizer settled). A judgement-based gate clears on a scanner exit code from the plugin's own scripts plus a distinct reviewer-agent verdict with file:line findings; an external scanner is optional additional evidence (FR-221).

OQ-2: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Gap-3 push grant and gap-6 revision-loop cap settled). The cap is 10 with two consecutive LGTMs as the normal pass; at the cap the orchestrator escalates with continue, waive, or abort (FR-218).

OQ-3: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Audit-logging stores settled (per-access split, rotation and retention, confirmation-store writer)). Size-based rotation replaces the 500-line cap, carries the prior segment's final chain hash into each new segment, and keeps segments at least 12 months; the rotation size is an estimate (NFR-032).
OQ-4: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Audit-logging stores settled (per-access split, rotation and retention, confirmation-store writer)). The two-file split of FR-227 is ratified as written.

OQ-5: Settled. Security-critical controls may fail closed on a malformed configuration while a profile is enforced; an absent configuration runs log-only (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, Compliance profile flags, enforced by default).

OQ-6: Settled. An access to a tagged path with no recorded purpose is logged unstated and flagged, never denied on the missing purpose alone (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, FERPA/HIPAA purpose capture, missing-purpose handling, and governance path protection; FR-230).

OQ-7: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Judgement-gate evidence and the /do human authorizer settled). The authorizer is the user who approved the plan, recorded as a reference to that approval and never message text; an autonomous or unapproved action records none with a reason (FR-227).

OQ-8: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Severity-policy basis and SARIF writer settled). The /do orchestrator writes the SARIF file; the reviewer stays read-only; uploading to GitHub falls under the FR-214 confirmation rule (FR-241).

OQ-9: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, OQ-9 resolved; FERPA control reframed, HIPAA scope tightened). HIPAA: FR-232 is verified against 45 CFR 164.312(b) as one required technical safeguard that records and supports review, not full HIPAA compliance. FERPA: the internal access log (FR-230) is general governance support and does not implement 34 CFR 99.32; FR-246 adds disclosure recordation for outbound education-record data and is the only control cited against 99.32.

OQ-10: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Audit-logging stores settled (per-access split, rotation and retention, confirmation-store writer)). A UserPromptSubmit hook writes the confirmation store as JSONL under a path in .agent/ protected under FR-245; the FR-214 guard reads it with file reads alone (FR-242). Refined (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, PN-10 pending-action store split and token lifetime settled): the store is a directory with confirmations.jsonl (hook-only, denied to every tool caller) and pending.jsonl (main-session /do writable, denied to every subagent); the token is single-use and time-expiring, with the window an estimate until measured (FR-242, FR-245).

OQ-11: Resolved. A hook writes the session purpose record from a purpose the user declares, and the access-logging hooks read it; with no declared purpose the log records unstated and flags the record (FR-247).

OQ-12: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30: Severity policy approved, re-approved by 2026-10-31: Severity policy approved). The user approved severity-policy.md version draft-2 (first approved at draft-1, superseded). The policy basis was settled earlier (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Severity-policy basis and SARIF writer settled); a rule may block on severity only after the FR-238 advisory baseline (FR-237).

OQ-13: Settled (Group A; DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-25). A default release-check run reports the last stored evaluation scoreboard and never runs the suite; an on-request run goes through the Group A harness (FR-273, FR-274).
